issue.title: [experiment][consumer] Test invisible consumption of generated knowledge
issue.body:
<!-- proto-ui:issue-governance:20261122:750:v1 -->

## 2026-11-22 当前代码核对

Agent: ChatGPT，按当前用户授权核对与治理。审计截止 [`a8bf56087`](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/commit/a8bf56087e5836e3c14c153cafbd796bd98bff37)；各项执行证据保留其实际 SHA。

核对基线：[`2c7eae25357d`](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/commit/2c7eae25357d0c5bae29bd5e92caae3a4ea39730)。

- [x] **可复用前置基础已存在**：当前[生成消费者测试](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/blob/2c7eae25357d0c5bae29bd5e92caae3a4ea39730/packages/compiler/test/observable-consumer.test.ts)与[实验记录框架](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/blob/2c7eae25357d0c5bae29bd5e92caae3a4ea39730/benchmarks/interaction/README.md)已在 main。它们仅支撑后续选取真实 artifact。
- [ ] 为本实验绑定实际输出、版本、分发方式与复现 consumer 项目，并执行不提供 Proto UI 内部 onboarding 的完整 discovery/install → use/customize/debug → ship 旅程。
- [ ] 记录失败、耗时、内部知识需求、代码改动与 escape hatch，并给出限定结论；现有 calibration／#734 不能充作本实验结果，原研究仍开放。

主线增量核对截止 [`a8bf56087e58`](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/commit/a8bf56087e5836e3c14c153cafbd796bd98bff37)；本段已执行的测试仍绑定 `2c7eae25357d`，不重标为新 main 运行。

---

## Context

This experiment tests whether protocol knowledge can travel through an ordinary generated artifact when its consumer does not need to study Proto UI's internal model. Do not invent a public package or component subset. On 2026-09-27 the active generated-target work is restricted to a Button path in [#732](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/issues/732), with [PR #736](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/pull/736) open; that is a candidate scope, not a completed or released consumer surface.

## Research question / hypothesis

Can a developer or Agent who does not know or care that Proto UI exists complete an ordinary `discover/install → use → customize → debug → ship` task using a generated artifact, with little or no Proto UI-specific knowledge?

A neutral result includes cases where generated output is hard to consume, escape hatches are frequent, or consumers must understand internal concepts.

## Experimental setup

**Prerequisite:** choose a real generated artifact subset available from a completed, reproducible Compiler/consumer pipeline, currently expected to be limited to Button if #732/#736 (or a reviewed successor) supplies it. Record exact output, target framework/version, package/distribution method and supported behavior. If no clean consumer artifact exists, leave this Issue blocked; do not substitute a mock library, hand-written component, or planned API.

Give developers or Agents with no Proto UI onboarding a normal consumer task covering discovery/install, import and use, customization, one realistic debugging change, and a production-like build/ship check. Do not mention Proto UI in the task unless its unavoidable provenance is revealed by the artifact. Keep task, environment, framework version, initial app, and time window consistent. Do not provide hidden internal docs or implementation assistance. If using more than one consumer, record prior framework/library experience.

Where useful and fair, include a familiar reference package using the same task and environment as a calibration baseline; it is optional and must not become a proxy for overall product quality. Do not require consumers to prefer the Proto-generated artifact.

## Baseline / control

The primary baseline is a fresh consumer project with no prior Proto UI knowledge, using the selected generated artifact and ordinary public instructions. Record the task environment and consumers' prior experience. A reference library run, if included, is reported separately and only for the matched task subset.

## Measurements

Measure task completion rate, time to first successful use, time and steps through each journey stage, amount of Proto UI-specific knowledge required, escape-hatch frequency and reason, generated-output edits/customizations, whether consumers can explain and modify generated code, debugging success, ship/build failures, and any point where internals become necessary. Preserve unsuccessful and abandoned runs.

## Expected artifacts

Artifact and package provenance; reproducible consumer fixture/instructions; exact task prompt and framework/toolchain; sanitized participant/Agent experience profile; event/task log; actual consumer code changes; success/failure and escape-hatch table; any actual output captures needed to support rendered claims; limitations/confounders; and supported / weakened / inconclusive / falsified interpretation.

## Known limitations / confounders

A narrow Button experiment cannot establish a whole-library experience. Package maturity, docs quality, framework familiarity, generated-code style, artifact provenance visibility, participant skills, task realism, and local tooling affect results. Consumer task completion does not prove business-level usability, overall UX, or suitability for arbitrary composition. The generated artifact is not automatically a product commitment.

## Completion criteria

- [ ] The measured artifact is real, its exact supported scope and provenance are documented, and another operator can reproduce the consumer setup.
- [ ] The journey is measured from discovery through a ship/build check; completion, failures, time, internals knowledge, code modifications and escape hatches are recorded.
- [ ] Results include cases where the consumer must learn Proto UI internals or cannot complete the task; no preference/satisfaction result is required.
- [ ] Limitations and confounders are documented and conclusions are bounded to the artifact/host/task that was exercised.
- [ ] If the artifact prerequisite is not met, the Issue remains staged and blocked without claiming an experimental outcome.

## Related work and dependencies

- Staged behind the generated consumer path in [#732](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/issues/732) and [PR #736](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/pull/736), or an equivalent reviewed artifact path.
- [#734](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/issues/734) covers the interaction-knowledge skill and three-path evidence; this experiment isolates ordinary consumption without Proto UI-specific onboarding.
- [#514](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/issues/514) is an Agent Harness dogfood matrix, not evidence that a public generated consumer artifact exists.
- Second phase after generated artifacts are usable; does not block release work.

## Agent evidence

Sanitized request paraphrase: test whether Proto UI knowledge creates value in an ordinary consumer workflow where the internal protocol can remain invisible. This is a plan only; no consumer run or product usability claim is made. For execution, upload actual generated-output/consumer captures when supporting rendered behavior and retain source-bound task traces; evidence debt remains until a real artifact is exercised.

<!-- proto-ui-radar-20260928:consumer -->
## Research follow-up — choose the consumer job before the product (2026-09-28)

The supplied opportunity notes suggest shadcn-style Web Components and cross-framework starters. Keep them as candidate applications of this experiment, not new library commitments. The existing Button consumer slice should not wait for a five-component port, a complete page, or another compiler target.

When selecting a follow-on task, attach a small evidence record: the concrete user job, dated firsthand source, current workaround, existing alternatives, switching cost, and why the current supply is insufficient. Distinguish an organization maintaining the same design system across applications from a developer who only needs one framework. Repeated links to one project are one evidence cluster; product launches, stars and a successful demo do not establish adoption demand. Unverified port-size or popularity figures from the notes are leads, not selection evidence.

Keep two outcomes separate:

- **Consumption:** can someone install, use, customize and debug the real artifact without learning Proto UI? That remains this Issue's primary experiment.
- **Maintenance economics:** if two real targets later exist, apply the same small semantic change and record target-specific code, tests, review and repair work, separately from shared compiler investment. Do not infer lower marginal maintenance cost from visually similar output or generated line count. This comparison is optional and does not add a second-target prerequisite.

If an existing library or explicit documentation solves the selected job with comparable effort, retain that result and defer the proposed product. Actual reusable gaps should return to #377 or their current component/Adapter owner, not a parallel port backlog. #754 may provide evidence about safe customization, but is not an additional dependency for the initial consumer study.

### Agent evidence for this addition

Sanitized request paraphrase: place demand-led product ideas in existing consumer research without turning speculative opportunities into implementation commitments. This addition is a proposed selection and interpretation method, based on the supplied notes and the live issue scope. Evidence disposition: **partial**; no external participant study, validated market-size estimate, generated-artifact run or maintenance-cost measurement is claimed. Task-level demand records and applicable real consumer captures remain execution work. Original scope, artifact prerequisites, milestone and ownership are preserved.

comments.body_html:
Suggested extension — make demand evidence a first-class outcome

The current consumer experiment answers whether a generated artifact can be consumed without learning Proto UI. That is necessary but not sufficient for the broader product question: does the artifact solve a job that somebody was already trying to solve?

The existing research follow-up points in this direction; I suggest treating the demand record as an explicit companion artifact whenever a follow-on consumer target is selected.

Demand record for each candidate job

Before building beyond the current Button slice, record:

  • the concrete user/Agent job in plain language;
  • dated firsthand evidence that the job exists;
  • the current workaround and its recurring cost;
  • existing libraries/tools that already solve it, if any;
  • why those alternatives are insufficient for this user/job;
  • switching/adoption cost;
  • what behavior would count as changing behavior because the artifact exists (installing it, keeping it, extending it, shipping it, replacing a workaround, etc.).

Prefer evidence of repeated effort or active search over stars, launch attention, or theoretical fit. A valid outcome is that an existing solution already satisfies the job cheaply enough and the proposed Proto UI-derived artifact should not be built.

Keep three questions separate

  1. Consumption: can someone discover/install/use/customize/debug/ship the artifact without Proto UI knowledge? (current primary scope)
  2. Demand: would someone choose to use it for a real pre-existing job rather than because the experiment asked them to?
  3. Maintenance economics: once adopted, does shared semantic ownership reduce repeated target-specific maintenance work?

Do not collapse successful task completion into evidence of demand, and do not infer demand from architectural elegance or generated-output quality.

Useful completion signal for future product experiments

For any candidate such as shadcn-style Web Components or cross-framework generated packages, the strongest evidence would be an external or independently selected consumer who was already looking for that outcome and changes their workflow because the artifact is available. Failure to observe that is also a result and should constrain product investment.
